items.title: DEV.3.2 - Distributed per-endpoint lock and cross-process admission (Postgres)
items.note: AUTOMATED_VALIDATED 2026-08-30. Split from distributed_endpoint_lock_and_job_store per the contract (docs/history/phase/DEV3_2_DISTRIBUTED_ENDPOINT_LOCK.md) into the device-safety half. New utils/coordinator_backend.py: CoordinatorBackend protocol, InMemoryCoordinatorBackend (prior CollectionCoordinator logic moved verbatim, plus two incidental bug fixes -- dead _endpoint_locks removed, budget_snapshot() undercounting above capacity 1 fixed), PostgresCoordinatorBackend (session-level pg_advisory_lock per endpoint on a dedicated per-job connection -- released by the server itself if the connection dies, no TTL/heartbeat -- plus a counted per-vendor budget gate and HMAC-derived lock keys so no device identity reaches Postgres), verify_postgres_backend_ready (fail-closed startup preflight detecting a transaction-pooling proxy), try_acquire_scheduler_lock (gates the scheduler read-evaluate-write cycle). CollectionCoordinator is now a thin backend-delegating shell; select_coordinator_backend() in collection_executor.py reads SECURITYEXPERT_COORDINATOR_BACKEND (memory default / postgres), wired into main.py with a clean parser.error on failure. Evidence, all against a real local PostgreSQL 16 (not mocked): a real child OS process admitted first, a second independent backend instance coalesced onto it (no second session opened) -- AC-1; the child was SIGKILLed and the endpoint was reclaimed with no TTL/heartbeat, the stale row marked orphaned -- AC-3; the preflight was manually verified against a real pgbouncer 1.22 in pool_mode=transaction and correctly refused to start (AC-5), with its two failure-detection branches also covered deterministically via a mocked driver in the committed suite. tests/test_dev3_2_distributed_endpoint_lock.py: 20 tests, all passing (includes the real cross-process kill test and a real cross-process scheduler-lock contention test). Full suite: 654 passed / 3 skipped / 2 failed (both pre-existing/unrelated) -- net +20, zero regressions. requirements-postgres.txt (optional, not in the base image) + .env.example document the opt-in. Concurrency budget value unchanged at 1. Real-environment validation against an actual multi-container deployment hitting a real Check Point MDS remains owed before DONE/REAL_ENV_VALIDATED -- server-blocked (DEPLOY.1, external). Blocks per_vendor_worker_split. Extends cp_device_interaction_safety / collection_execution_coordinator into the multi-process world.

items.title: Investigate intermittent local immutable evidence-store PermissionError
items.note: AUTOMATED_VALIDATED 2026-08-30. Root cause: ConfigEvidenceStore._ensure_blob already retried os.replace on transient (OSError, PermissionError) for the content-addressed blob write, but the snapshot-directory publish right after it (os.replace(tmp_dir, final_dir) in _write_snapshot) had no retry at all -- a single AV/indexer lock there failed the whole snapshot write, surfacing as the LOCAL_IMMUTABLE_EVIDENCE_STORE / local_filesystem_permission_or_lock failure already classified in configuration/panorama_config_collector.py. Fix: extracted the existing bounded retry (3 attempts, 0.1s exponential backoff) into ConfigEvidenceStore._replace_with_retry and applied it to the directory-publish os.replace call; _ensure_blob's own loop is unchanged. Two new regression tests in tests/test_phase0_6_0a4_3_2_content_addressed_storage.py: a transient-then-success case (self-heals, snapshot still lands) and a persistent-lock case (still raises cleanly, no leftover .tmp- directory). No collector/network/CAS-schema/UI change. Evidence: py -m pytest -q: 552 passed, 2 skipped, 2 failed (both pre-existing and reproduced identically on the unmodified baseline -- test-order pollution in test_phase0_6_1c_discovery_capability_ui.py / test_phase0_7_5_compliance_trend.py, out of scope for this fix; baseline is 550 passed / same 2 failures, so this change is a net +2 passing from the new regression tests with zero regressions).

VSX __vsid_ convention, unresolvable id = request-time error before any device contact) + vendor dispatch (RecoveryCollector protocol) + run_recovery_collection (admission-coordinated per target via a caller-supplied run_under_admission hook, one target's failure never aborts the batch) -- the same orchestration a CLI, the scheduler, or a future UI action all call identically. panorama/panorama_recovery_collector.py: PAN device-state export (contract §7.1) IMPLEMENTED -- read class, gate-documented before this build, D2 resolved; reuses panorama_runtime_runner.get_api_key/_tls_verify_setting verbatim, session-reuse cached per host, never retries a 403. checkpoint/checkpoint_recovery_collector.py: CP Gaia backup stays a typed blocked stub (RecoveryCollectionBlockedError naming D3, unresolved) -- CORRECTED 2026-08-30 during a main-branch merge: the P0 cp_device_interaction_safety audit that used to co-gate this actually closed 2026-08-25, before this build; D3 alone is the real remaining blocker. utils/collection_executor.py: ALLOWLISTED_WORKFLOWS gains 'recovery-pan' (NOT 'recovery-cp'); ScheduledWorkflow gains an additive optional 'targets' field (omitted = 'all', schema version unchanged, every existing policy file's meaning preserved) -- corrected an over-strict architecture-doc claim that scheduled recovery needed distributed_endpoint_lock_and_job_store (DEV.3.2/3.3); that only applies once collection splits across multiple containers, not under the current single-process DEV.3.1 coordinator every other scheduled workflow already uses. main.py: --recovery-collect/--recovery-vendor/--recovery-gateways (thin dispatch only, zero collection logic) + _scheduler_workflow_argv extended for recovery-pan. utils/recovery_validation.py (RB.4): validate_artifact runs V1 (hash/size) / V2 (gzip-openable, non-empty, XML-well-formed for pan_running_config) / V3 (cross-check unified.json: device present, data_state fresh, version match -- NOT_APPLICABLE not PASS when inventory or artifact version is absent/unknown, never invented); attach_restore_proof is the only path that can ever set V4/RESTORE_PROVEN, requires a complete real restore_proof. utils/recovery_store.revalidate_artifact wires it into the store (decrypt in memory only, rewrite manifest.validation). main.py --recovery-validate (offline, exit 1 if ANY individual check across all held artifacts FAILs -- deliberately not driven by the top-line verdict alone, since a V2-only failure still reports verdict=INTACT). Real bug caught by tests and fixed: the initial level-advancement logic let an all-NOT_APPLICABLE level (e.g. V3 with no matching inventory) silently count as 'passed'; fixed to require at least one actual PASS. 85 new tests total (19 RB.4 tests/test_rb4_recovery_validation.py, 25 RB.2/RB.3 tests/test_rb2_recovery_collect.py incl. PAN collector against a fixture HTTP transport only -- never live -- and CP stub verification; existing tests/test_phase0_6_1c_collection_executor.py::test_allowlisted_workflows_are_read_only updated for recovery-pan). Manually verified end-to-end via main.main() and a real --scheduler-once run (fixture unified.json, fake credentials): CP path fails closed immediately naming the exact blocker; PAN path resolves targets, acquires admission, attempts the real (unreachable-in-sandbox) network call, fails gracefully per-target, exit 1; unresolvable gateway fails before any device contact; scheduler correctly dispatches 'recovery-pan' with its targets list through the identical --recovery-collect CLI path. py -m pytest -q: 741 passed, 3 skipped, 2 pre-existing unrelated failures (unchanged). Repository privacy gate PASS/0. RB.3 (CP) remains blocked; RB.2's PAN configuration-XML export (§7.2, secondary/companion artifact) not yet implemented; software_version for PAN artifacts recorded as the honest 'unknown' sentinel since unified.json carries no version field and inventing a new undocumented device command to fetch one was explicitly avoided.

items.title: Render harness breaks on happy-dom >= 20 (window.eval removed)
items.target: before RB.5 (or any next UI build)
items.note: DISCOVERED 2026-08-30 during backup_recovery_architecture (incidental, not caused by it; recorded not fixed, per the do-not-silently-broaden-scope law). tools/render-harness/check-render.mjs line ~55 executes the report's inline <script> via window.eval(). happy-dom 20.12.0 does not expose window.eval, so the harness dies with 'TypeError: window.eval is not a function' BEFORE it asserts anything about the page -- a false FAIL that looks like a product regression. Reproduced by running `bun install` in tools/render-harness/ on a machine without a pre-existing node_modules: this sandbox's bun also rewrote bun.lock lockfileVersion 2 -> 1 (reverted, not committed), i.e. the committed lockfile is not pinning happy-dom the way it does on the author's box. Impact: tests/test_html_render_harness.py::test_headless_navigation_smoke skipif's when node_modules is absent, so the breakage is INVISIBLE until someone installs deps -- and AGENTS.md makes this harness mandatory for any templates/app.js/style.css/payload-builder change. RB.5 (Recovery UI module) is exactly such a change. Fix direction: pin happy-dom explicitly in package.json (not just the lockfile) and/or replace window.eval with a Function-constructor or <script>-injection execution path; tools/render-harness/check_render_playwright.py already exists as the Playwright/Chromium fallback (render_harness fallback build) and may be the more durable primary.

items.title: CE.1 - User-authored compliance check engine (data-driven, evidence-only)
items.note:
AUTOMATED_VALIDATED 2026-08-29 (docs/history/phase/0_7_3_COMPLIANCE_CHECK_ENGINE.md sections 10-11). Shipped: utils/compliance_check_pack.py + utils/compliance_check_engine.py (pure), compliance_posture wiring (_subject_user_checks / _scoring_rows / check_packs / user_check_meta), control_assignment.extra_known_ids, UI user-defined + advisory badges + Explain source-pack/step lines. CE.1 crypto-source follow-up: build_compliance_posture(..., crypto_facts_by_subject); html_export threads the privacy-reviewed 0.7.0 fact groups so a check can assert over crypto_facts.<group>. pytest 516p/3s/0f; privacy gate PASS/0; render exit 0. CE.1 fast-follow #2 (2026-08-29, docs/history/phase/0_7_3_COMPLIANCE_CHECK_ENGINE.md section 12): build_compliance_posture(..., unified_inventory) + html_export threads the loaded unified.json; a subject joins its merged-inventory row(s) by normalised device identity, vendor-scoped (cp/vsx | panorama); unified.interfaces / unified.routes now resolve (unmatched -> None -> on_no_evidence); those two collections are load-restricted to present/absent/count_gte/count_lte and render a count-only observed so no interface address / route target enters the payload; pytest 529p/3s/0f. Original design note follows.

Design: docs/design/COMPLIANCE_CHECK_ENGINE.md (all decisions D1-D16 resolved 2026-08-29, section 10). The BackBox/Nipper model - a check is DATA (name + evidence source + expected pattern + verdict), matches -> compliant, else not. Buildable now: no server, no new device command. Task breakdown: (1) utils/compliance_check_pack.py - load_compliance_checks(data_root) -> CompliancePack from data/state/compliance_checks.json, schema v1, CompliancePackError, fail-closed: schema, id regex ^x_[a-z0-9_]+$ + uniqueness (D1/D15), every source namespace+selector known (D4/D13), every assert.op in the fixed set (D2), pattern compiles + passes the complexity linter + <=512 chars (D3), severity/frameworks well-formed, remediation block rejected as 'not yet supported' (section 11); missing file -> empty pack (D16); enabled:false -> inert. (2) utils/compliance_check_engine.py - resolve_source(subject_evidence, selector) with a hand-written tokenizer NS('.'SEGMENT)* , SEGMENT=KEY|KEY'['KEY'='VALUE']' , no eval / no new dep (D13); apply_assertion(value, assertion) -> bool|None (None=inconclusive) for present/absent/equals/not_equals/matches/not_match/any_match/none_match/gte/lte/in/not_in/count_gte/count_lte; regex behind a timeout+linter, timeout/error -> step UNKNOWN never PASS (D3); evaluate_check(subject_evidence, check) pure, evidence.steps[] with combine all|any (D5), no-evidence -> on_no_evidence (default UNKNOWN). (3) compliance_posture._subject_user_checks(...) after _subject_extended_controls, append to subject.extended_controls with control_class 'user_check' + pack {pack_id,pack_version,source}; applies_to miss -> omit + count in assignment.not_assigned (D14); mode advisory|enforced (D6) - advisory rows excluded from compliance_overview numerator AND denominator + framework coverage (D11). (4) control_assignment.py - extend the waiver known-id set with load_compliance_checks(...) ids so a dated waiver can target a user check (D7). (5) Payload: top-level check_packs [{pack_id,pack_version,source,checks,advisory_checks,enabled}] counts+ids only; per-check observed/expected per step for the 0.7.2 Explain panel; NEVER the pattern or raw selector (D12). (6) UI: a 'user-defined' badge + provenance line on user-check cards; framework chips + Explain reused unchanged. (7) --repository-privacy-check guard that data/state/compliance_checks.json is never committed (D16). (8) tests/test_phase0_7_3_compliance_check_engine.py - synthetic fixtures + a sample pack; pytest + --render-only; no network, no real-env gate. Reserves an optional remediation block for the write-capable future (section 11), rejected by the CE.1 validator.

items.title: CE.2 - Curated read-only command-primitive registry for checks
items.note: Design: docs/design/COMPLIANCE_CHECK_ENGINE.md section 5 (decision D8). configuration/command_primitives.py - a static registry; each entry is an individually 10-point-network-device-command-gate-reviewed READ-ONLY command (vendor, shell/context, timeout, retry, max frequency per endpoint, session reuse, per-primitive redaction rule). The admission coordinator runs referenced primitives once per device per run inside the 1-per-vendor budget + CP stage cooldown; output stored as a new evidence artifact class, redacted by the primitive rule, exposed to the engine as source namespace primitive.<primitive_id>. Opt-in --compliance-probe mode only (like --cp-config-probe); promote to a normal-run stage only after a real-environment validation gate. Checks reference primitive.<id>, never a raw command string. cp_device_interaction_safety (P0) closed 2026-08-25 (corrected 2026-08-30 -- CURRENT_STATE.md/AI_HANDOVER.md had kept it listed as an open blocker after closure); remaining prerequisite is each primitive's own network-device command gate review + a real-environment validation gate. No write / config-changing command is ever admitted at current maturity.

items.title: CE.3 - Browser check editor + signed distributable org check packs
items.note: Design: docs/design/COMPLIANCE_CHECK_ENGINE.md section 6 (decision D9). A Compliance-module check editor: name a check, pick the evidence source from a browsable tree of WHAT WAS ACTUALLY COLLECTED (no blank text box), choose an operator, enter the expected value/pattern, test it LIVE against the last run (which subjects pass/fail), preview the coverage delta, save; every save audited (who/when/before/after). Server writes the same compliance_checks.json shape (or its Postgres equivalent). Signed org packs: detached signature + a publisher trust store so an org distributes vetted check packs without a product release (the dynamic/signed-pack direction of the 0.6.6B / 0.7.0 rule packs); invalid/untrusted -> rejected, fail-closed. CIS/PCI/BDDK starter packs shipped as signed builtin-adjacent packs the operator enables. Requires the app server + DEPLOY.1A OIDC/RBAC (only an authorised role creates/edits/loads checks) + a persistent store. Signing mechanism specifics deferred to the DEPLOY.1 security workstream (deploy1_oidc_viewer / secrets vault).

items.title: CE.4 - Remediation checks (write-capable, HARD-GATED)
items.note: Design: docs/design/COMPLIANCE_CHECK_ENGINE.md sections 11-12. The product end-state is a write-capable device administration platform; the check model reserves an OPTIONAL remediation { primitive: <write_primitive_id>, parameters, verify_after: [steps] } block, unused and validator-rejected in CE.1-CE.3. CE.4 lets the engine, on an operator-authorised in-window run, execute the write primitive, re-run verify_after (reusing the CE.1 source/assert grammar verbatim), record an immutable audit entry, and auto-rollback on verify failure. A future REMEDIABLE sub-state on FINDING is additive. HARD-GATED on every prerequisite in docs/design/FAILOVER_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md section 10 - the same bar as failover_controlled_execution / OP.2: mature VERIFY/TRACE/RECOVER, the DEPLOY.1 server, DEPLOY.1A OIDC + an RBAC OPERATE role + full audit, the CP device-interaction-safety audit, the network-device command gate for every read AND write primitive, and a signed change-management / safety review with the network-security leads. No implementation until all are met.
